summary: Threads run parts of a program at the same time. When two threads change the same variable, synchronized or an AtomicInteger makes sure no update is lost.
notes: sold++ is not one step. It reads, adds, and writes, and another thread can run in between. That is a race condition.
pool.shutdown() then pool.awaitTermination(...) waits for every task, the same job join() does for one Thread.
incrementAndGet() on an AtomicInteger is safe without synchronized.
pitfall: A race condition may not show up on every run, so code that passed once can still be wrong. Calling run() instead of start() on a Thread runs the code on the main thread, so no second thread is created.
